NKJV.1: In those days there was no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking an inheritance for itself to dwell in; for until that day their inheritance among the tribes of Israel had not fallen to them.
NKJV.2: So the children of Dan sent five men of their family from their territory, men of valor from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and search it. They said to them, “Go, search the land.” So they went to the mountains of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and lodged there.
NKJV.3: While they were at the house of Micah, they recognized the voice of the young Levite. They turned aside and said to him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? What do you have here?”
NKJV.4: He said to them, “Thus and so Micah did for me. He has hired me, and I have become his priest.”
NKJV.5: So they said to him, “Please inquire of God, that we may know whether the journey on which we go will be prosperous.”
NKJV.6: And the priest said to them, “Go in peace. The presence of the LORD be with you on your way.”
NKJV.7: So the five men departed and went to Laish. They saw the people who were there, how they dwelt safely, in the manner of the Sidonians, quiet and secure. There were no rulers in the land who might put them to shame for anything. They were far from the Sidonians, and they had no ties with anyone.
NKJV.8: Then the spies came back to their brethren at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brethren said to them, “What is your report?”
NKJV.9: So they said, “Arise, let us go up against them. For we have seen the land, and indeed it is very good. Would you do nothing? Do not hesitate to go, and enter to possess the land.
NKJV.10: When you go, you will come to a secure people and a large land. For God has given it into your hands, a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth.”
NKJV.11: And six hundred men of the family of the Danites went from there, from Zorah and Eshtaol, armed with weapons of war.
NKJV.12: Then they went up and encamped in Kirjath Jearim in Judah. (Therefore they call that place Mahaneh Dan to this day. There it is, west of Kirjath Jearim.)
NKJV.13: And they passed from there to the mountains of Ephraim, and came to the house of Micah.
NKJV.14: Then the five men who had gone to spy out the country of Laish answered and said to their brethren, “Do you know that there are in these houses an ephod, household idols, a carved image, and a molded image? Now therefore, consider what you should do.”
NKJV.15: So they turned aside there, and came to the house of the young Levite man—to the house of Micah—and greeted him.
NKJV.16: The six hundred men armed with their weapons of war, who were of the children of Dan, stood by the entrance of the gate.
NKJV.17: Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up. Entering there, they took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molded image. The priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men who were armed with weapons of war.
NKJV.18: When these went into Micah’s house and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molded image, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”
NKJV.19: And they said to him, “Be quiet, put your hand over your mouth, and come with us; be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be a priest to the household of one man, or that you be a priest to a tribe and a family in Israel?”
NKJV.20: So the priest’s heart was glad; and he took the ephod, the household idols, and the carved image, and took his place among the people.
NKJV.21: Then they turned and departed, and put the little ones, the livestock, and the goods in front of them.
NKJV.22: When they were a good way from the house of Micah, the men who were in the houses near Micah’s house gathered together and overtook the children of Dan.
NKJV.23: And they called out to the children of Dan. So they turned around and said to Micah, “What ails you, that you have gathered such a company?”
NKJV.24: So he said, “You have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and you have gone away. Now what more do I have? How can you say to me, ‘What ails you?’ ”
NKJV.25: And the children of Dan said to him, “Do not let your voice be heard among us, lest angry men fall upon you, and you lose your life, with the lives of your household!”
NKJV.26: Then the children of Dan went their way. And when Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back to his house.
NKJV.27: So they took the things Micah had made, and the priest who had belonged to him, and went to Laish, to a people quiet and secure; and they struck them with the edge of the sword and burned the city with fire.
NKJV.28: There was no deliverer, because it was far from Sidon, and they had no ties with anyone. It was in the valley that belongs to Beth Rehob. So they rebuilt the city and dwelt there.
NKJV.29: And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel. However, the name of the city formerly was Laish.
NKJV.30: Then the children of Dan set up for themselves the carved image; and Jonathan the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.
NKJV.31: So they set up for themselves Micah’s carved image which he made, all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh.

CSB17.1: In those days, there was no king in Israel, <sup>ⓓ</sup> and the Danite tribe was looking for territory to occupy. <sup>ⓔ</sup> Up to that time no territory had been captured by them among the tribes of Israel.
CSB17.2: So the Danites sent out five brave men <sup>ⓕ</sup> from all their clans, from Zorah and Eshtaol, <sup>ⓖ</sup> to scout <sup>ⓗ</sup> out the land and explore it. They told them, “Go and explore the land.” They came to the hill country of Ephraim as far as the home of Micah and spent the night there.
CSB17.3: While they were near Micah’s home, they recognized the accent of the young Levite. So they went over to him and asked, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? What is keeping you here?”
CSB17.4: He told them, “This is what Micah has done for me: He has hired me, and I became his priest.”
CSB17.5: Then they said to him, “Please inquire of God <sup>ⓘ</sup> for us to determine if we will have a successful journey.”
CSB17.6: The priest told them, “Go in peace. The LORD is watching over the journey you are going on.”
CSB17.7: The five men left and came to Laish. They saw that the people who were there were living securely, in the same way as the Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting. There was nothing lacking <sup>[1]</sup> in the land and no oppressive ruler. They were far from the Sidonians, having no alliance with anyone. <sup>[2]</sup>
CSB17.8: When the men went back to their relatives at Zorah and Eshtaol, <sup>ⓙ</sup> their relatives asked them, “What did you find out?”
CSB17.9: They answered, “Come on, let’s attack them, for we have seen the land, and it is very good. Why wait? Don’t hesitate to go and invade and take possession of the land!
CSB17.10: When you get there, you will come to an unsuspecting people and a spacious land, for God has handed it over to you. It is a place where nothing on earth is lacking.” <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.11: Six hundred Danites departed from Zorah and Eshtaol armed with weapons of war.
CSB17.12: They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim <sup>ⓛ</sup> in Judah. This is why the place is still called the Camp of Dan <sup>[3]</sup> today; it is west of Kiriath-jearim.
CSB17.13: From there they traveled to the hill country of Ephraim and arrived at Micah’s house.
CSB17.14: The five men who had gone to scout out the land of Laish told their brothers, “Did you know that there are an ephod, household gods, and a carved image and a silver idol <sup>[4]</sup> in these houses? Now think about what you should do.”
CSB17.15: So they detoured there and went to the house of the young Levite at the home of Micah and greeted him.
CSB17.16: The six hundred Danite men were standing by the entrance of the city gate, armed with their weapons of war.
CSB17.17: Then the five men who had gone to scout out the land went in and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the silver idol, <sup>[5]</sup> while the priest was standing by the entrance of the city gate with the six hundred men armed with weapons of war.
CSB17.18: When they entered Micah’s house and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the silver idol, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”
CSB17.19: They told him, “Be quiet. Keep your mouth shut. <sup>[6]</sup> <sup>ⓜ</sup> Come with us and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one person or for you to be a priest for a tribe and family in Israel?”
CSB17.20: So the priest was pleased and took his ephod, household idols, and carved image, and went with the people.
CSB17.21: They prepared to leave, putting their dependents, livestock, and possessions in front of them.
CSB17.22: After they were some distance from Micah’s house, the men who were in the houses near it were mustered and caught up with the Danites.
CSB17.23: They called to the Danites, who turned to face them, and said to Micah, “What’s the matter with you that you mustered the men?”
CSB17.24: He said, “You took the gods I had made and the priest, and went away. What do I have left? How can you say to me, ‘What’s the matter with you? ’”
CSB17.25: The Danites said to him, “Don’t raise your voice against us, or angry men will attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives.”
CSB17.26: The Danites went on their way, and Micah turned to go back home, because he saw that they were stronger than he was.
CSB17.27: After they had taken the gods Micah had made and the priest that belonged to him, they went to Laish, to a quiet and unsuspecting people. They killed them with their swords and burned the city. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.28: There was no one to rescue them <sup>ⓐ</sup> because it was far from Sidon and they had no alliance with anyone. It was in a valley that belonged to Beth-rehob. They rebuilt the city and lived in it.
CSB17.29: They named the city Dan, after the name of their ancestor Dan, who was born to Israel. The city was formerly named Laish.
CSB17.30: The Danites set up the carved image for themselves. Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Moses, <sup>[7]</sup> and his sons were priests for the Danite tribe until the time of the exile from the land. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.31: So they set up for themselves Micah’s carved image that he had made, and it was there as long as the house of God was in Shiloh. <sup>ⓒ</sup>

NLT.1: Now in those days Israel had no king. And the tribe of Dan was trying to find a place where they could settle, for they had not yet moved into the land assigned to them when the land was divided among the tribes of Israel.
NLT.2: So the men of Dan chose from their clans five capable warriors from the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol to scout out a land for them to settle in. When these warriors arrived in the hill country of Ephraim, they came to Micah’s house and spent the night there.
NLT.3: While at Micah’s house, they recognized the young Levite’s accent, so they went over and asked him, “Who brought you here, and what are you doing in this place? Why are you here?”
NLT.4: He told them about his agreement with Micah and that he had been hired as Micah’s personal priest.
NLT.5: Then they said, “Ask God whether or not our journey will be successful.”
NLT.6: “Go in peace,” the priest replied. “For the LORD is watching over your journey.”
NLT.7: So the five men went on to the town of Laish, where they noticed the people living carefree lives, like the Sidonians; they were peaceful and secure. The people were also wealthy because their land was very fertile. And they lived a great distance from Sidon and had no allies nearby.
NLT.8: When the men returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their relatives asked them, “What did you find?”
NLT.9: The men replied, “Come on, let’s attack them! We have seen the land, and it is very good. What are you waiting for? Don’t hesitate to go and take possession of it.
NLT.10: When you get there, you will find the people living carefree lives. God has given us a spacious and fertile land, lacking in nothing!”
NLT.11: So 600 men from the tribe of Dan, armed with weapons of war, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.
NLT.12: They camped at a place west of Kiriath-jearim in Judah, which is called Mahaneh-dan to this day.
NLT.13: Then they went on from there into the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah.
NLT.14: The five men who had scouted out the land around Laish explained to the others, “These buildings contain a sacred ephod, as well as some household idols, a carved image, and a cast idol. What do you think you should do?”
NLT.15: Then the five men turned off the road and went over to Micah’s house, where the young Levite lived, and greeted him kindly.
NLT.16: As the 600 armed warriors from the tribe of Dan stood at the entrance of the gate,
NLT.17: the five scouts entered the shrine and removed the carved image, the sacred ephod, the household idols, and the cast idol. Meanwhile, the priest was standing at the gate with the 600 armed warriors.
NLT.18: When the priest saw the men carrying all the sacred objects out of Micah’s shrine, he said, “What are you doing?”
NLT.19: “Be quiet and come with us,” they said. “Be a father and priest to all of us. Isn’t it better to be a priest for an entire tribe and clan of Israel than for the household of just one man?”
NLT.20: The young priest was quite happy to go with them, so he took along the sacred ephod, the household idols, and the carved image.
NLT.21: They turned and started on their way again, placing their children, livestock, and possessions in front of them.
NLT.22: When the people from the tribe of Dan were quite a distance from Micah’s house, the people who lived near Micah came chasing after them.
NLT.23: They were shouting as they caught up with them. The men of Dan turned around and said to Micah, “What’s the matter? Why have you called these men together and chased after us like this?”
NLT.24: “What do you mean, ‘What’s the matter?’” Micah replied. “You’ve taken away all the gods I have made, and my priest, and I have nothing left!”
NLT.25: The men of Dan said, “Watch what you say! There are some short-tempered men around here who might get angry and kill you and your family.”
NLT.26: So the men of Dan continued on their way. When Micah saw that there were too many of them for him to attack, he turned around and went home.
NLT.27: Then, with Micah’s idols and his priest, the men of Dan came to the town of Laish, whose people were peaceful and secure. They attacked with swords and burned the town to the ground.
NLT.28: There was no one to rescue the people, for they lived a great distance from Sidon and had no allies nearby. This happened in the valley near Beth-rehob. Then the people of the tribe of Dan rebuilt the town and lived there.
NLT.29: They renamed the town Dan after their ancestor, Israel’s son, but it had originally been called Laish.
NLT.30: Then they set up the carved image, and they appointed Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Moses, as their priest. This family continued as priests for the tribe of Dan until the Exile.
NLT.31: So Micah’s carved image was worshiped by the tribe of Dan as long as the Tabernacle of God remained at Shiloh.

NRSVCE.1: In those days there was no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking for itself a territory to live in; for until then no territory among the tribes of Israel had been allotted to them.
NRSVCE.2: So the Danites sent five valiant men from the whole number of their clan, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to explore it; and they said to them, “Go, explore the land.” When they came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, they stayed there.
NRSVCE.3: While they were at Micah’s house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they went over and asked him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? What is your business here?”
NRSVCE.4: He said to them, “Micah did such and such for me, and he hired me, and I have become his priest.”
NRSVCE.5: Then they said to him, “Inquire of God that we may know whether the mission we are undertaking will succeed.”
NRSVCE.6: The priest replied, “Go in peace. The mission you are on is under the eye of the LORD.”
NRSVCE.7: The five men went on, and when they came to Laish, they observed the people who were there living securely, after the manner of the Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting, lacking nothing on earth, and possessing wealth. Furthermore, they were far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with Aram.
NRSVCE.8: When they came to their kinsfolk at Zorah and Eshtaol, they said to them, “What do you report?”
NRSVCE.9: They said, “Come, let us go up against them; for we have seen the land, and it is very good. Will you do nothing? Do not be slow to go, but enter in and possess the land.
NRSVCE.10: When you go, you will come to an unsuspecting people. The land is broad — God has indeed given it into your hands — a place where there is no lack of anything on earth.”
NRSVCE.11: Six hundred men of the Danite clan, armed with weapons of war, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol,
NRSVCE.12: and went up and encamped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. On this account that place is called Mahaneh-dan to this day; it is west of Kiriath-jearim.
NRSVCE.13: From there they passed on to the hill country of Ephraim, and came to the house of Micah.
NRSVCE.14: Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land (that is, Laish) said to their comrades, “Do you know that in these buildings there are an ephod, teraphim, and an idol of cast metal? Now therefore consider what you will do.”
NRSVCE.15: So they turned in that direction and came to the house of the young Levite, at the home of Micah, and greeted him.
NRSVCE.16: While the six hundred men of the Danites, armed with their weapons of war, stood by the entrance of the gate,
NRSVCE.17: the five men who had gone to spy out the land proceeded to enter and take the idol of cast metal, the ephod, and the teraphim. The priest was standing by the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men armed with weapons of war.
NRSVCE.18: When the men went into Micah’s house and took the idol of cast metal, the ephod, and the teraphim, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”
NRSVCE.19: They said to him, “Keep quiet! Put your hand over your mouth, and come with us, and be to us a father and a priest. Is it better for you to be priest to the house of one person, or to be priest to a tribe and clan in Israel?”
NRSVCE.20: Then the priest accepted the offer. He took the ephod, the teraphim, and the idol, and went along with the people.
NRSVCE.21: So they resumed their journey, putting the little ones, the livestock, and the goods in front of them.
NRSVCE.22: When they were some distance from the home of Micah, the men who were in the houses near Micah’s house were called out, and they overtook the Danites.
NRSVCE.23: They shouted to the Danites, who turned around and said to Micah, “What is the matter that you come with such a company?”
NRSVCE.24: He replied, “You take my gods that I made, and the priest, and go away, and what have I left? How then can you ask me, ‘What is the matter?’”
NRSVCE.25: And the Danites said to him, “You had better not let your voice be heard among us or else hot-tempered fellows will attack you, and you will lose your life and the lives of your household.”
NRSVCE.26: Then the Danites went their way. When Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back to his home.
NRSVCE.27: The Danites, having taken what Micah had made, and the priest who belonged to him, came to Laish, to a people quiet and unsuspecting, put them to the sword, and burned down the city.
NRSVCE.28: There was no deliverer, because it was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with Aram. It was in the valley that belongs to Beth-rehob. They rebuilt the city, and lived in it.
NRSVCE.29: They named the city Dan, after their ancestor Dan, who was born to Israel; but the name of the city was formerly Laish.
NRSVCE.30: Then the Danites set up the idol for themselves. Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Moses, and his sons were priests to the tribe of the Danites until the time the land went into captivity.
NRSVCE.31: So they maintained as their own Micah’s idol that he had made, as long as the house of God was at Shiloh.

NIV.1:
Danites Settle in Laish
In those days Israel had no king.
And in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking a place of their own where they might settle, because they had not yet come into an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
NIV.2:
So the Danites sent five warriors from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out the land and explore it. These men represented all their clans. They told them, “Go, explore the land.”
The men entered the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah, where they spent the night.
NIV.3: When they were near Micah’s house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they turned in there and asked him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?”
NIV.4: He told them what Micah had done for him, and said, “He has hired me and I am his priest.”
NIV.5: Then they said to him, “Please inquire of God to learn whether our journey will be successful.”
NIV.6: The priest answered them, “Go in peace. Your journey has the Lord’s approval.”
NIV.7: So the five men left and came to Laish, where they saw that the people were living in safety, like the Sidonians, unsuspecting and secure. And since their land lacked nothing, they were prosperous. Also, they lived a long way from the Sidonians and had no relationship with anyone else.
NIV.8: When they returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their brothers asked them, “How did you find things?”
NIV.9: They answered, “Come on, let’s attack them! We have seen that the land is very good. Aren’t you going to do something? Don’t hesitate to go there and take it over.
NIV.10: When you get there, you will find an unsuspecting people and a spacious land that God has put into your hands, a land that lacks nothing whatever.”
NIV.11: Then six hundred men from the clan of the Danites, armed for battle, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.
NIV.12: On their way they set up camp near Kiriath Jearim in Judah. This is why the place west of Kiriath Jearim is called Mahaneh Dan to this day.
NIV.13: From there they went on to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah’s house.
NIV.14: Then the five men who had spied out the land of Laish said to their brothers, “Do you know that one of these houses has an ephod, other household gods, a carved image and a cast idol? Now you know what to do.”
NIV.15: So they turned in there and went to the house of the young Levite at Micah’s place and greeted him.
NIV.16: The six hundred Danites, armed for battle, stood at the entrance to the gate.
NIV.17: The five men who had spied out the land went inside and took the carved image, the ephod, the other household gods and the cast idol while the priest and the six hundred armed men stood at the entrance to the gate.
NIV.18: When these men went into Micah’s house and took the carved image, the ephod, the other household gods and the cast idol, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”
NIV.19: They answered him, “Be quiet! Don’t say a word. Come with us, and be our father and priest. Isn’t it better that you serve a tribe and clan in Israel as priest rather than just one man’s household?”
NIV.20: Then the priest was glad. He took the ephod, the other household gods and the carved image and went along with the people.
NIV.21: Putting their little children, their livestock and their possessions in front of them, they turned away and left.
NIV.22: When they had gone some distance from Micah’s house, the men who lived near Micah were called together and overtook the Danites.
NIV.23: As they shouted after them, the Danites turned and said to Micah, “What’s the matter with you that you called out your men to fight?”
NIV.24: He replied, “You took the gods I made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have? How can you ask, ‘What’s the matter with you?’”
NIV.25: The Danites answered, “Don’t argue with us, or some hot-tempered men will attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives.”
NIV.26: So the Danites went their way, and Micah, seeing that they were too strong for him, turned around and went back home.
NIV.27: Then they took what Micah had made, and his priest, and went on to Laish, against a peaceful and unsuspecting people. They attacked them with the sword and burned down their city.
NIV.28:
There was no one to rescue them because they lived a long way from Sidon and had no relationship with anyone else. The city was in a valley near Beth Rehob.
The Danites rebuilt the city and settled there.
NIV.29: They named it Dan after their forefather Dan, who was born to Israel—though the city used to be called Laish.
NIV.30: There the Danites set up for themselves the idols, and Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses, and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan until the time of the captivity of the land.
NIV.31: They continued to use the idols Micah had made, all the time the house of God was in Shiloh.

NET.1: In those days Israel had no king. And in those days the Danite tribe was looking for a place to settle, because at that time they did not yet have a place to call their own among the tribes of Israel.
NET.2: The Danites sent out from their whole tribe five representatives, capable men from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it. They said to them, “Go, explore the land.” They came to the Ephraimite hill country and spent the night at Micah’s house.
NET.3: As they approached Micah’s house, they recognized the accent of the young Levite. So they stopped there and said to him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? What is your business here?”
NET.4: He told them what Micah had done for him, saying, “He hired me and I became his priest.”
NET.5: They said to him, “Seek a divine oracle for us, so we can know if we will be successful on our mission.”
NET.6: The priest said to them, “Go with confidence. The LORD will be with you on your mission.”
NET.7: So the five men journeyed on and arrived in Laish. They noticed that the people there were living securely, like the Sidonians do, undisturbed and unsuspecting. No conqueror was troubling them in any way. They lived far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone.
NET.8: When the Danites returned to their tribe in Zorah and Eshtaol, their kinsmen asked them, “How did it go?”
NET.9: They said, “Come on, let’s attack them, for we saw their land and it is very good. You seem lethargic, but don’t hesitate to invade and conquer the land.
NET.10: When you invade, you will encounter unsuspecting people. The land is wide! God is handing it over to you — a place that lacks nothing on earth!”
NET.11: So six hundred Danites, fully armed, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.
NET.12: They went up and camped in Kiriath Jearim in Judah. (To this day that place is called Camp of Dan. It is west of Kiriath Jearim.)
NET.13: From there they traveled through the Ephraimite hill country and arrived at Micah’s house.
NET.14: The five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish said to their kinsmen, “Do you realize that inside these houses are an ephod, some personal idols, a carved image, and a metal image? Decide now what you want to do.”
NET.15: They stopped there, went inside the young Levite’s house (which belonged to Micah), and asked him how he was doing.
NET.16: Meanwhile the six hundred Danites, fully armed, stood at the entrance to the gate.
NET.17: The five men who had gone to spy out the land broke in and stole the carved image, the ephod, the personal idols, and the metal image, while the priest was standing at the entrance to the gate with the six hundred fully armed men.
NET.18: When these men broke into Micah’s house and stole the carved image, the ephod, the personal idols, and the metal image, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”
NET.19: They said to him, “Shut up! Put your hand over your mouth and come with us! You can be our adviser and priest. Wouldn’t it be better to be a priest for a whole Israelite tribe than for just one man’s family?”
NET.20: The priest was happy. He took the ephod, the personal idols, and the carved image and joined the group.
NET.21: They turned and went on their way, but they walked behind the children, the cattle, and their possessions.
NET.22: After they had gone a good distance from Micah’s house, Micah’s neighbors gathered together and caught up with the Danites.
NET.23: When they called out to the Danites, the Danites turned around and said to Micah, “Why have you gathered together?”
NET.24: He said, “You stole my gods that I made, as well as this priest, and then went away. What do I have left? How can you have the audacity to say to me, ‘What do you want?’”
NET.25: The Danites said to him, “Don’t say another word to us, or some very angry men will attack you, and you and your family will die.”
NET.26: The Danites went on their way; when Micah realized they were too strong to resist, he turned around and went home.
NET.27: Now the Danites took what Micah had made, as well as his priest, and came to Laish, where the people were undisturbed and unsuspecting. They struck them down with the sword and burned the city.
NET.28: No one came to the rescue because the city was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with anyone. The city was in a valley near Beth Rehob. The Danites rebuilt the city and occupied it.
NET.29: They named it Dan after their ancestor, who was one of Israel’s sons. But the city’s name used to be Laish.
NET.30: The Danites worshiped the carved image. Jonathan, descendant of Gershom, son of Moses, and his descendants served as priests for the tribe of Dan until the time of the exile.
NET.31: They worshiped Micah’s carved image the whole time God’s authorized shrine was in Shiloh.
